features.title: Trajectory Supervisor
features.hypothesis: The trajectory supervisor's one LLM call on the cannotMakeProgress() stall edge redirects enough stalled runs into recovery to justify its extra cost, latency and tokens.
features.corpusNote: Single-turn verdict was CUT. The supervisor_conversation slice (turn 1 stalls, supervisor asks, turn 2 the user answers, run recovers) is now in `slice` but DORMANT — the driver keys re-runs off progress.json, not the manifest, so to re-run this feature a human must reset eval/reports/audit/progress.json's trajectory-supervisor entry (seedsDone:0, finalized:false) AND flip status back to queued. Deliberately left done so it does not auto-re-run on Haiku while the model-pinning issue is open. The multi-node decomposed _run_planner path is still adapter-side / separate.

features.title: The 11-layer harness vs. a bare model loop
features.hypothesis: Running the full 11-layer harness every turn produces materially better task outcomes than a bare ReAct loop, enough to justify the whole subsystem's per-turn cost.
features.corpusNote: First pass (CUT, d124361) was invalid: the 20 persistent_tool_failure tasks fire only for the one-loop flagOn arm (proposer wrap), not for bare, so flagOn ran a forced stall while bare ran clean — the entire multi_step gap. excludeSlice drops the supervisor / failure-match stress fixtures; the runner skip-guard also drops any injected-failure task bare can't honour. So this measures non-failure task quality only; recovery-under-failure for bare is a coverage gap (F1b) until an MCP-server-level injection lands. Model: Sonnet (F6 confirmed the first pass was Sonnet; the Haiku label was a modelUsage parsing bug). See the internal plan.

features.title: One-loop harness-driven proposer
features.hypothesis: Letting the harness drive tool calls in-loop (ASSISTANT_ONE_LOOP=enabled) beats post-hoc bookkeeping over an already-finished reply, retroactively validating the 2026-09-06 default flip.
features.corpusNote: First pass (CUT, 976ecd2) was invalid: persistent_tool_failure injection fires only for the one-loop flagOn arm, not for the pre-one-loop baseline (no oneLoopProposer to wrap), so flagOn ran a forced stall while baseline ran clean — that is the recoveryRate 0.72->0.29. excludeSlice + the skip-guard drop those tasks. F3 (no empty reply on stall) also landed. So this measures the one-loop rewire on non-failure tool tasks; the recovery-under-failure question needs F1b. Model: Sonnet (F6). See the internal plan.

features.title: Semantic contradiction check
features.hypothesis: The checkForContradictions LLM call catches enough real paraphrased / cross-framing belief contradictions that the always-on lexical negation-pair check misses to pay for its per-belief-set-growth cost.
features.corpusNote: Single-turn slice (both halves in one prompt) plus audit_contradiction_multiturn — belief stated turn 1, unrelated beliefs turns 2-3, paraphrased contradiction on the last turn, with control tasks (legitimate change over time) that must not be false-flagged.

features.title: LLM injection detection on tool output
features.hypothesis: detectInjectionLikelyWithLLM catches tool-output prompt-injection the deterministic pattern pass misses, often enough to justify the per-output latency and without a false-positive tax on benign instruction-like content.
features.corpusNote: Within-turn mechanism; slice measures both true-positive (slip-past payloads) and false-positive (benign instruction-like files). Add fetched-page tool outputs, not just file reads (A5 code-path gap, separate from turn count).

features.title: Semantic failure-mode match
features.hypothesis: checkSemanticFailureMatch recognises known failure patterns described in different words often enough to earn its per-miss call and improve recovery routing.
features.corpusNote: Paraphrased-failure classification is testable single-turn. Whether it improves recovery is a compressed proxy (bounded re-answer loop). Injected-symptom mechanism is artificial but isolates the classifier; note the caveat in the entry.

features.title: Semantic criterion coverage
features.hypothesis: The checkSemanticCriterionCoverage LLM call recognises success criteria a reply satisfies in different words than the plan states them, removing false 'criterion not met' findings the reviewer's substring check raises, often enough to justify +1 call per unmatched criterion.
features.corpusNote: Within-turn mechanism, but the shipped bridge (harness-bridge.ts) passes only NON_CHECKABLE_DEFAULT_CRITERION to runtime.run(), for which the hook returns false with no LLM call; plan successCriteria never reach it. Expect no arm differential: the entry must be published scoped to 'the hook is unreachable from a product turn', not as a verdict on paraphrase recognition. Any spurious-finding effect is seen by the single-turn grader only through retries/escalations.

features.title: Semantic change reviewer
features.hypothesis: The semanticChangeReviewer LLM call catches proposed changes that conflict in meaning with a held high-confidence belief, which the reviewer's lexical check misses, often enough to justify +1 call per proposed change and without blocking compatible changes.
features.corpusNote: Within-turn once the belief is held; the belief-establishing turn is part of the task (pre-seeded memory is not a supported corpus shape, so every task states the constraint on turn 1 and proposes the conflicting change on turn 3). Caveats: conflicts against beliefs from a much earlier session are out of scope; the hook is skipped for a change that reads like a coding fact (looksLikeCodingFact) and runs only after the mechanical review passed, so the slice uses natural-language domains; whether the constraint reaches a >= 0.8-confidence belief depends on fact extraction, so a null arm differential may mean the belief was never held rather than that the call is worthless.

features.title: Model-inferred facts
features.hypothesis: Facts the classifier infers from a message (statesDurableFacts, source model_inferred) are recalled correctly on later turns often enough to justify recording them, without a wrong-memory tax from hypotheticals and retracted statements.
features.corpusNote: Mechanism is cross-turn; slice covers within-session recall over 3 turns. Cross-session persistence and the /memory confirm queue are not exercised. The flag gates consumption of the classifier's facts (buildTurnFacts), not the classifier call. Caveat: the raw transcript is still in context on turn 3, so a null differential may mean the transcript already carried the fact rather than that recording it adds nothing. Turn-1 phrasings were checked against the lexical pass (extractFactsFromTurn returns nothing), so only the model_inferred path can record them.

features.title: Up-front decomposition + task reframing
features.hypothesis: Decomposing a multi-part request into a task graph and reframing each task with an LLM call completes more of the requested parts than treating the request as one task, at acceptable extra cost.
features.corpusNote: Within-turn; the harness executes each task against one draft reply, so decomposition changes what is verified more than what is generated, and a null quality differential is a plausible outcome. One flag (AUDIT_DECOMPOSITION) covers both mechanisms: decomposition is the classifier's decomposedTasks output (bundled into the mandatory classifyTurnIntent call, so it adds no LLM call of its own), and the reframe call only ever fires on the single-task path, so they cannot be toggled independently and stay one manifest entry. Caveats: the flag gates consumption of decomposedTasks, not the classifier call; the reframe call additionally requires a non-LOW risk classification and a coding-fact-shaped message, so the read-only fixture tasks mostly exercise decomposition, not reframing; a task the classifier routes into plan mode would bypass this hook.

features.title: The verification layer
features.hypothesis: Always-on mechanical verification of every result catches defective or unsupported results before they are accepted, cutting confidently-wrong replies enough to justify running on every turn.
features.corpusNote: Mechanical layer; single-turn covers within-turn defects (a stated total or average contradicting its own samples, conflicting sources, a missing file, an empty search, a pending figure) plus 2 correct-result controls. Eval-only ablation: AUDIT_VERIFICATION=0 makes HarnessRuntime skip verify() and treat each iteration as an empty pass; the shipped default cannot disable it and the Python twin is untouched. Caveats: an arm without verification also loses the recovery cycles verification triggers, so the entry must report recovery and cost alongside success; verification checks against the turn's own evidence, not ground truth, so a defect the model copies verbatim from a file may pass in both arms; the ablated arm also has no answerClaim verification_status (no_evidence/unverified_attempted).
